# Ateles: chronic tax vs acute crisis (frame-product-argument)

## Subject

What the solo technical founder-operator ICP tolerates daily versus what converts them to adopt Ateles.

## Summary

Acute leads: an untraceable, unattributed high-blast agent action already taken (a merge, a payment, a message) converts harder than the chronic tax of manual multi-chat coordination and context loss, because the chronic tax is a cost the operator has already decided to absorb.

## Body

Chronic: The operator coordinates multiple agent chats by hand, opening a new one per task and hoping concurrent ones do not conflict. Nothing persists between sessions, so context is re-explained every time — project state, prior decisions, constraints. Coordination logic accretes as a growing CLAUDE.md and scattered shell scripts rather than any declared workflow. This is diffuse, cumulative, and survivable: an operator absorbs it for months because each single instance costs only a few extra minutes of re-explaining or a bit of copy-paste glue, and nothing about it looks urgent on any given day (docs/foundation/charter.md, origin/main: 'coordination is ad-hoc, starting a multi-agent workflow means opening chats by hand and hoping they do not conflict, and the operator pays the difference in bespoke scripts and manual sync').

Acute: The failure, at the level the operator actually feels it, is discovering that you cannot trust you would find out if something had gone wrong — so you are back to watching, the exact thing delegation was supposed to remove. Either you babysit every agent's work across every domain, personal and professional, or you find out after the fact that one of them took a consequential action — a merge, a payment, an outbound message — in a way you would have caught had you been looking. The concrete trigger is discovering that action with no reconstructable record of who authorized it or under what scope, because the agent acted under the operator's own shared identity with no distinct attribution. But the record, the checkpoint that would have stopped it for approval, and the distinct attributed identity are each how the operator gets to stop watching — not the benefit itself; the operator's own ruling on this (2026-09-21) is that "the 'record of who authorized it' is in a way an important piece of making all of that work but not my top-level benefit per se." The cost is discoverable and specific: an action the operator cannot explain, defend, or undo cleanly, surfacing exactly when it matters (a bad merge that shipped, a payment that should have been checkpointed, an email sent that should not have gone out).

Leads: ACUTE LEADS. The chronic tax (manual sequencing, context loss) is the more relatable and easier pain to write copy about, but per the register's own standing rule (plan ent_98ef9d45f8a6896fed408f8f, decision 'problem_leads_the_hero': the hero states the problem, and per the frame-product-argument skill's chronic/acute doctrine) a reader who recognizes a tax they have already decided to absorb has no reason to act today. The acute crisis — discovering you cannot trust you would know if something went wrong, so you are back to babysitting — is the strongest single qualifier: it is the moment the operator can name the problem precisely and go looking for a fix. The specific trigger that makes the crisis legible — an untraceable, unattributed high-blast action already taken — is also the failure mode the competitor test (research_finding ent_f8271efcdb842076a5147929) found NOT claimable by a generic orchestration framework, which has no concept of authority or accountability; that finding still grounds why this crisis is a real qualifier and not just a vivid anecdote, it now supports the benefit-level statement above rather than standing in as the lead itself. The existing settled headline candidate for this lead, from the same decision register, is 'Agents are cheap. Organizations are not.' (parent problem statement, plan ent_98ef9d45f8a6896fed408f8f overview) — this pain analysis supplies the chronic/acute mechanics under that headline; it does not propose a different headline.

Reviewed by: pm.

## Gaps

No field-verified customer research (icp_signal / customer_development_note) exists for Ateles on this Neotoma instance to corroborate which pain actually converts a real prospect — both the chronic and acute descriptions and the lead call are derived from the product's own stated rationale for existing (charter.md, README.md), not from interviews or outreach signal. This should be treated as a reasoned hypothesis to validate against real conversations, not a confirmed finding.
